plan_a_advantages: Consistent recovery with frequent easy runs.
Simple and easy to follow, requiring minimal planning.
plan_b_advantages: Includes specific workouts designed to improve speed and threshold.
Incorporates a longer run to build endurance relevant to trail races.
More varied workout types (tempo, aerobic) to stimulate different physiological adaptations.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses heavily on easy runs, which can be beneficial for recovery, it lacks any structured efforts to improve speed or threshold. Plan B incorporates a tempo run and a longer, controlled effort, directly addressing the goal of increasing running speed and building sustainable strength – key components for trail running performance. The inclusion of a longer run also better simulates the demands of trail races, whereas Plan A’s runs are consistently short.
